metadata.title: JavaScript Minifier
metadata.description: Minify JavaScript to reduce file size

faqs.question: What is JavaScript minification?
faqs.answer: JavaScript minification reduces the size of a JS file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

faqs.question: How do I minify JavaScript?
faqs.answer: Paste your JavaScript code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

faqs.question: Does minification affect JavaScript functionality?
faqs.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for execution. The functionality of your JavaScript remains unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.

faqs.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
faqs.answer: The reduction depends on the original JavaScript. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact JS may see only a small reduction.

faqs.question: Is my JavaScript sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Can I minify large JavaScript files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large JavaScript files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

intro.title: What is a JavaScript Minifier?
paragraphs: A JavaScript minifier is a free online tool for reducing the size of JavaScript files by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage. All minification happens in the browser.

sections.title: How to minify JavaScript
paragraphs: Paste your JavaScript code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

sections.title: How minification works
paragraphs: Minification removes characters that are not needed in JavaScript: multiple spaces become a single space, comments are removed, and line breaks are removed. It does not obfuscate variable names or change the logic.

metadata.title: JWT Decoder
metadata.description: Decode and inspect JSON Web Tokens (JWT), with signature verification support

faqs.question: What is a JWT?
faqs.answer: A JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe format for representing claims between parties. It consists of three parts — header, payload and signature — encoded in Base64URL and separated by dots (.).

faqs.question: How do I decode a JWT?
faqs.answer: Paste the JWT into the input field. The tool decodes it automatically and displays the header and payload parts in a readable format. It also checks whether the token has expired.

faqs.question: Can this tool verify JWT signatures?
faqs.answer: No. This tool only decodes JWTs without verifying the signature. Verification requires the key used to sign the token. Always verify JWTs on the server side.

faqs.question: Are JWTs secure?
faqs.answer: JWTs can be used securely, but must be implemented correctly. Always verify the signature, check the expiration time, do not store sensitive data in the payload (it is Base64 encoded, not encrypted), and use HTTPS in transit.

faqs.question: What are common use cases for JWTs?
faqs.answer: JWTs are commonly used for authentication (after login, the server returns a JWT that the client stores), information exchange (securely transferring information between parties) and authorization (representing user permissions).

faqs.question: Is decoding a JWT safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool decodes JWTs locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server. However, do not store sensitive information in client-side JWTs, because anyone can decode them.

faqs.question: What are meta tags?
faqs.answer: Meta tags are tags in the head of an HTML document that provide metadata about the page, such as the title, description, keywords and Open Graph information. They are not displayed on the page but are used by search engines and social media platforms.

faqs.question: How do I use the meta tag generator?
faqs.answer: Fill in the form fields: title, description, keywords, image and so on. The tool generates the HTML meta tags in real time. Copy the generated code and paste it into the <head> section of your HTML.

faqs.question: What are Open Graph tags?
faqs.answer: Open Graph tags control how your page appears when shared on Facebook, LinkedIn and other social platforms. They define the title, description, image and other elements shown when sharing.

faqs.question: What are Twitter card tags?
faqs.answer: Twitter card tags control how your page appears when shared on Twitter. They are similar to Open Graph tags but specific to Twitter, and can enable special formats such as large images or app install cards.

faqs.question: Are meta tags important for SEO?
faqs.answer: Yes. While meta keywords no longer directly affect rankings, meta titles and descriptions are important for SEO. They appear in search results and can influence click-through rates. Open Graph tags also affect social sharing.

faqs.question: Can I generate tags for multiple platforms?
faqs.answer: Yes. The generator creates standard meta tags, Open Graph tags (for Facebook, LinkedIn, etc.) and Twitter card tags. All tags are included in the generated code.

sections.title: How to generate meta tags

sections.title: Understanding Open Graph

sections.title: Understanding Twitter cards
paragraphs: Twitter card tags control how your page appears when shared on Twitter. They define the card type (summary, large image, etc.) and its content. They complement the Open Graph tags.

metadata.title: Robots.txt Generator
metadata.description: Generate a robots.txt file for your website

faqs.question: What is robots.txt?
faqs.answer: robots.txt is a text file placed in the root directory of a website. It tells search engine crawlers which pages or files may or may not be crawled on your website.

faqs.question: How do I use the robots.txt generator?
faqs.answer: Select the crawlers to allow (such as Googlebot, Bingbot), add allow and disallow rules, and specify the sitemap location. The tool generates a robots.txt file for you to download or copy.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Disallow and Allow directives?
faqs.answer: Disallow tells crawlers not to access specific paths. Allow overrides Disallow and permits access to specific sub-paths. By default, everything is allowed if no rules are specified.

faqs.question: Should I block all crawlers?
faqs.answer: Usually not. You generally only want to block specific directories (like /admin/ or /private/). Blocking all crawlers (User-agent: * Disallow: /) removes your website from search results.

faqs.question: Can robots.txt protect sensitive pages?
faqs.answer: No. robots.txt is publicly accessible and anyone can read it. It does not prevent users from accessing pages. For real protection, use password protection or server-side authentication.

faqs.question: Should I include a Sitemap directive?
faqs.answer: Yes. Including Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml helps search engines find your sitemap and index your website better.

intro.title: What is a Robots.txt Generator?
paragraphs: A robots.txt generator is a free online tool for creating robots.txt files. It helps you control how search engine crawlers interact with your website, specify which paths are allowed or disallowed, and include sitemap references. All generation happens in the browser.

sections.title: How to create robots.txt
paragraphs: Select the crawler to configure (or use * for all crawlers). Add allow and disallow rules to specify which paths may or may not be crawled. Add your sitemap URL. Copy the generated robots.txt content and upload it to the root directory of your website.

sections.title: Understanding the syntax
paragraphs: robots.txt uses the User-agent directive to specify which crawler a rule applies to. The Disallow directive blocks access to paths. The Allow directive overrides Disallow. The Sitemap directive specifies the sitemap location.

sections.title: Common patterns
items: Blocking all crawlers from the admin area
Allowing a specific crawler to access everything
Blocking access to private directories
Specifying the sitemap location
Setting different rules for different crawlers

metadata.title: Timestamp Converter
metadata.description: Convert between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates

faqs.question: What is a Unix timestamp?
faqs.answer: A Unix timestamp is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC (known as the "epoch"). It is a standard way to represent time in computer systems and programming.

faqs.question: How do I convert a timestamp to a date?
faqs.answer: Enter the Unix timestamp in the timestamp field. The tool instantly converts it to a human-readable date and time, displayed in your local timezone and UTC.

faqs.question: How do I convert a date to a timestamp?
faqs.answer: Pick a date and time with the date picker or enter it manually. The tool generates the corresponding Unix timestamp.

faqs.question: Are timestamps in seconds or milliseconds?
faqs.answer: The tool shows both second (10-digit) and millisecond (13-digit) timestamps. Most systems use seconds, but JavaScript's Date.now() returns milliseconds.

faqs.question: What is the current timestamp?
faqs.answer: The current timestamp is shown at the top of the tool and updates in real time every second. It displays the current Unix time in seconds and milliseconds.

faqs.question: How are timezones handled?
faqs.answer: Timestamps are always based on UTC. The converted date is displayed in both your local timezone and UTC for easy reference.

intro.title: What is a Unix Timestamp Converter?
paragraphs: A Unix timestamp converter is a free online tool for converting between Unix timestamps and human-readable dates. It also shows the live current timestamp. All conversions happen in the browser.

sections.title: Understanding Unix time
paragraphs: Unix time (also called epoch time) is the number of seconds elapsed since January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC. It ignores leap seconds and has exactly 86400 seconds per day.

metadata.title: URL Encoder
metadata.description: Encode or decode URLs and query string parameters

faqs.question: What is URL encoding?
faqs.answer: URL encoding (also called percent-encoding) converts special characters into a format of % followed by two hexadecimal digits. For example, a space becomes %20. This is necessary to safely transmit characters in URLs.

faqs.question: How do I encode a URL?
faqs.answer: Paste the URL or text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts special characters into their percent-encoded equivalents.

faqs.question: How do I decode a URL?
faqs.answer: Paste the encoded URL into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts percent-encoded characters back to their original format.

faqs.question: What is the difference between component encoding and full URI encoding?
faqs.answer: Component encoding (encodeURIComponent) encodes all characters except alphanumerics and -_.!~*'(). Full URI encoding (encodeURI) does not encode characters that are already valid in URLs, such as :/?#[]@.

faqs.question: Why is URL encoding needed?
faqs.answer: URLs can only use a subset of ASCII characters. URL encoding lets you safely include spaces, Unicode characters and special characters that could conflict with URL syntax.

faqs.question: Is URL encoding safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool encodes and decodes URLs locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

intro.title: What is a URL Encoder/Decoder?
paragraphs: A URL encoder/decoder is a free online tool for encoding and decoding URLs and query parameters. It supports both component encoding and full URI encoding modes. All processing happens in the browser.

paragraphs: Paste the URL or text into the input field. Select the encode mode (component or full URI). The tool converts special characters into percent-encoded format.

sections.title: How to decode a URL
paragraphs: Paste the encoded URL into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts percent-encoded characters back to their original format.

sections.title: Understanding the encoding modes
paragraphs: Component encoding (encodeURIComponent) encodes all characters except alphanumerics and a few special characters. Full URI encoding (encodeURI) preserves URL structure characters and only encodes characters that are not allowed in URLs.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce sales tax?

metadata.description: Calculate Body Mass Index in imperial or metric units, view BMI categories and healthy weight ranges.

faqs.question: What is BMI?
faqs.answer: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a measure of body fat based on height and weight. It's calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared. BMI is a screening tool, not a diagnostic measure of body fat or health.

faqs.question: What are the BMI categories?
faqs.answer: Underweight: below 18.5. Normal weight: 18.5-24.9. Overweight: 25.0-29.9. Obese: 30.0 and above. These categories are based on World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines for adults.

faqs.question: Is BMI accurate?
faqs.answer: BMI has limitations. It can't distinguish between muscle and fat mass, so muscular people may have a "high" BMI without having high body fat. It also doesn't account for age, sex, bone density, or fat distribution. Use it as one reference point, not a complete health picture.

faqs.question: Does BMI apply to children?
faqs.answer: For children, BMI uses age- and sex-specific percentiles rather than fixed adult categories. Pediatric BMI calculators account for normal growth patterns. This calculator is designed for adults (20+).

metadata.title: Compound Interest Calculator
metadata.description: See how your money grows with compound interest and regular contributions.

faqs.question: What is compound interest?
faqs.answer: Compound interest is interest calculated on both the initial principal and accumulated interest. Unlike simple interest, your earnings generate their own earnings, producing exponential growth over time.

faqs.question: How does compounding frequency affect returns?
faqs.answer: More frequent compounding (daily vs. annual) produces slightly higher returns because interest starts earning interest sooner. The difference is most noticeable with high rates and long time periods.

faqs.question: What is the Rule of 72?
faqs.answer: The Rule of 72 estimates how long it takes to double your money: divide 72 by the annual interest rate. At a 7% annual return, your money doubles roughly every 10.3 years (72 / 7 = 10.3).

faqs.question: Are the results guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. This calculator assumes a fixed rate, which suits savings accounts and bonds. Investment returns (stocks, funds) vary year to year. Use average historical returns for long-term projections.
